predecessors.note: Second Peace of Thorn, 19 October 1466: the western half of the Order's Prussia (Pomerelia, the Chełmno Land, Elbing, Marienburg). The Order kept Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) and the east as a Polish fief.

predecessors.note: The Confederation, a rebel state of 1454-1466, pledged allegiance to Casimir IV on 6 March 1454 and was incorporated into Poland; its land becomes Royal Prussia.

predecessors.note: 1637: after Duke Bogislaw XIV died childless the Lauenburg and Bütow Land, held as a Polish fief by the Griffin dukes since 1466/1526, 'again became a terra of the Polish Crown' and joined the Pomeranian voivodeship (Lauenburg and Bütow Land page).

successors.note: Annexed in 1772 (West Prussia from 1773, with the Marienwerder district and the Netze District); Warmia is the prince-bishopric's.
Danzig and Thorn stayed Polish until 1793 (First Partition page: Prussia did not take them).

correction.text: Royal Prussia: Pomerelia (the Pomeranian voivodeship), the Chełmno Land with Toruń, Świecie, Grudziądz and Tuchola, and the Elbing and Marienburg district; without Warmia, the Lauenburg and Bütow Land and the Teutonic remainder round Marienwerder

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Royal Prussia row; it draws the area in its Teutonic Order and Kingdom of Poland shapes). Redrawn after review: the gazetteer region 'West Prussia' (Pomeranian + Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeships, 41,476 km2) was wrong, it left out Elbląg and drew Crown Kuyavia and Greater Poland (Włocławek, Inowrocław, Bydgoszcz), Słupsk, Lębork and Bytów. The shape is now the Pomeranian voivodeship minus the Słupsk/Lauenburg-Bütow polygon and minus the Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) district east of the Vistula, plus the Kuyavian-Pomeranian land of the Chełmno Land (a polygon north of the Vistula: Toruń, Chełmno, Świecie, Grudziądz, Tuchola, Brodnica), plus a 20 km disc at Elbląg minus the Warmia shape: about 21,250 km2 on the grid. 19 October 1466: Poland received 'Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and the Chełmno Land' and 'the region of Elbing, Marienburg, and the Bishopric of Warmia'; the eastern part 'remained with the Teutonic Order as a fief of the Polish Crown'. The Royal Prussia page: Marienburger Land with Elbing, Chełmno Land and Michałów Land (Chełmno voivodeship, Thorn), the Pomeranian voivodeship with Danzig; Kwidzyn (Marienwerder) 'formed Upper Prussia' and stayed with the Knights (Kwidzyn page: 'part of Poland as a fief held by the Teutonic Knights'). No area on the Royal Prussia page. Cross-check: the Pomeranian Voivodeship page gives 12,907 km2 for the voivodeship (its Lauenburg-Bütow years aside); the drawn Pomeranian part is 14,674 km2 on 253 km2 cells. Disc tests on the redrawn shape: Elbląg, Malbork, Gdańsk, Toruń, Grudziądz, Chojnice, Tuchola, Gniew inside; Włocławek, Inowrocław, Bydgoszcz, Słupsk, Lębork, Kwidzyn and the Warmia towns outside. Warmia has its own dossier (recognised as part of Poland 1466).

correction.text: Royal Prussia with the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba), 1637-1657

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 1637, after Duke Bogislaw XIV died childless, 'the land again became a terra of the Polish Crown' (Lauenburg and Bütow Land page; it joined the Pomeranian Voivodeship in 1641 there, 'from 1637 to 1657' on the Pomeranian Voivodeship page). The Land is drawn as a polygon of about 3,000 km2 (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba); the page gives no area.

correction.text: Royal Prussia: Pomerelia (the Pomeranian voivodeship), the Chełmno Land with Toruń, Świecie, Grudziądz and Tuchola, and the Elbing and Marienburg district; without Warmia, the Lauenburg and Bütow Land and the Teutonic remainder round Marienwerder

keyframe_review.note: 1657: the Treaty of Bydgoszcz, 'which amended the Treaty of Wehlau', granted the Lauenburg and Bütow Land as a fief to the Hohenzollerns of Brandenburg-Prussia; it is no longer drawn here. Prussia incorporated it in 1772 (not a Royal Prussian loss). Swedish occupation of 1626-1635 and 1655-1660 is in the ledger (hatched), not in this shape.

region.text: Royal Prussia: Pomerelia (the Pomeranian voivodeship), the Chełmno Land with Toruń, Świecie, Grudziądz and Tuchola, and the Elbing and Marienburg district; without Warmia, the Lauenburg and Bütow Land and the Teutonic remainder round Marienwerder

ledger.note: 19 October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn creates Royal Prussia. 'signed in the Hanseatic city of Thorn (Toruń) on 19 October 1466'; Poland receives Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and the Chełmno Land and the region of Elbing and Marienburg; infobox 'Established: 19 October 1466'. The Prussian Confederation had pledged allegiance to Casimir IV on 6 March 1454 ('Incorporation Act').

1569: the Union of Lublin integrates Royal Prussia fully into the Kingdom of Poland: 'Royal Prussia was integrated fully into the Kingdom of Poland' and its parliament 'was reduced to the status of a provincial assembly'; no border changes. Counted here as a change of status, not of land.

region.text: Marienburg, Dirschau, Mewe and Putzig, taken in 1626

ledger.note: July 1626: after landing at Pillau on 6 July 1626 the Swedes 'rapidly occupied Braniewo, Frombork, Elbląg, Orneta, and Malbork', then 'crossed the Vistula and took Tczew, Gniew, Oliwa and Puck'; Danzig held out. Month is the landing sequence's; the towns' individual dates are not on the page (Braniewo, Frombork, Orneta are Warmia's).
July 1626: the Swedes occupy Elbląg (Elbing), the town they keep until 1635.

region.text: Marienburg, Dirschau, Mewe and Putzig, taken in 1626

ledger.note: Truce of Altmark: 'In Royal Prussia, Sweden retained the towns of Braunsberg, Frauenberg, and Elbing', so Marienburg, Dirschau, Mewe and Putzig return to Poland. This page dates the truce 6 September 1629; the Truce of Altmark page says 26 September 1629 (16 September Old Style); the month is the same.

12 September 1635: the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf: 'the Swedes had to return the territories they occupied in Baltic Prussia' (Elbing, Memel, Pillau; the last two to the Elector of Brandenburg) and withdraw their garrisons. The page does not name Poland as recipient of Elbing; implied.

intersect.text: the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba)

region.text: the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba)

ledger.note: 1637: 'After Duke Bogislaw XIV died childless, the land again became a terra of the Polish Crown' (Lauenburg and Bütow Land page); the Pomeranian Voivodeship page has Bytów, Lębork and Łeba in the voivodeship 'from 1637 to 1657', the Land page from 1641. Duchy-of-pomerania books the 1466 gain from the Order; its loss in 1637 is not booked there.
Nov-Dec 1655: the Swedes take Toruń in their sweep of Royal Prussia; it 'was besieged from July 1, 1658' and capitulated on 30 December 1658. Month is the start of the page's 'Nov-Dec 1655' sweep.
Nov-Dec 1655: Graudenz (Grudziądz) taken in the sweep; captured by the Poles in August 1659.
Nov-Dec 1655: Brodnica taken in the sweep; its 'starving garrison surrendered in 1659'.

minus.text: Royal Prussia with the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (1637-1657)

region.text: nearly all of Royal Prussia except Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork, Nov-Dec 1655

ledger.note: The Deluge page: 'The Swedes took nearly all of Royal Prussia in Nov-Dec 1655, excluding Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork'; Elbląg is among the towns taken. By late 1656 they held only the right-bank half; Rinsk (12 October 1655) had let Brandenburg garrison Royal Prussia but excluded Gdańsk, Elbląg and Toruń.
Malbork 'not taken in the 1655 sweep', but listed as Swedish in autumn 1657 (siege continued in 1659); the date it fell is not on the page, so 1657 is the first listing.

intersect.text: the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba)

region.text: the Lauenburg and Bütow Land (Lębork, Bytów, Łeba)

ledger.note: 1657: 'The Treaty of Bydgoszcz, which amended the Treaty of Wehlau, granted it as a fief to the Hohenzollerns of Brandenburg-Prussia, on the terms the Griffins had enjoyed, in return for help against Sweden.' Brandenburg-prussia books the 1657 gain from the Commonwealth.
30 December 1658: Toruń capitulated after a siege from 1 July 1658.
1659: the starving Swedish garrison of Brodnica surrendered (month not on the page).
August 1659: Graudenz captured by the Poles.
3 May 1660: the Treaty of Oliva ends the war. The page does not list the return of Malbork (still besieged in 1659).

region.text: the Swedish-held remainder of Royal Prussia in 1660 (Elbing among it)

ledger.note: 3 May 1660: the Treaty of Oliva ends the war ('cost Poland most of Livonia'); the page names no change in Royal Prussia. Elbląg was blockaded by Polish-Brandenburgian troops and besieged from December 1659; the date it was handed back is not on the page.

region.text: Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn, annexed by Prussia in 1772

ledger.note: 1772: the First Partition. 'the former territory of Royal Prussia was annexed by the Kingdom of Prussia' (infobox 'Dissolved: 1 July 1772'; the partition treaty was signed on 5 August 1772 and the new province of West Prussia was formed in 1773, First Partition page). Prussia took 'Most of Polish Royal Prussia, including Ermland (Warmia)' (Warmia goes with prince-bishopric-of-warmia), about 36,000 km2 with the Netze District and northern Kuyavia, 'Not Danzig (Gdańsk) or Thorn (Toruń)'.

1772: Danzig and Thorn, left out of the partition ('Prussia did not take these cities'), stay with the Commonwealth; the Royal Prussia page has the rest of 'the former territory' annexed in 1793. Counterpart is my reading: the Commonwealth's Cliopatria row, to which the pair fall back.

region.text: Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn, annexed by Prussia in 1772

ledger.note: 1 July 1772: Royal Prussia ends as a Polish province; West Prussia succeeds it in the infobox.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War

zones.text: Royal Prussia: Pomerelia (the Pomeranian voivodeship), the Chełmno Land with Toruń, Świecie, Grudziądz and Tuchola, and the Elbing and Marienburg district; without Warmia, the Lauenburg and Bütow Land and the Teutonic remainder round Marienwerder

wars.outcome: Ended by the Second Peace of Thorn on 19 October 1466: the western half of the Order's state, with Pomerelia, the Chełmno Land, Elbing and Marienburg, goes to Poland; the east remains the Order's fief of the Polish Crown.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus landed at Pillau on 6 July 1626; the Truce of Altmark (September 1629) left Sweden Braunsberg, Frauenberg and Elbing in Royal Prussia until the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf (12 September 1635).
wars.note: Dates of the truce differ by page (6 or 26 September 1629).

wars.name: The Deluge (Second Northern War in Poland)

zones.text: Royal Prussia, nearly all taken by the Swedes in Nov-Dec 1655

wars.outcome: The Swedes took nearly all of Royal Prussia in Nov-Dec 1655 except Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork; Toruń fell back to the Poles on 30 December 1658, Graudenz in August 1659; the Treaty of Oliva of 3 May 1660 ended the war.
wars.note: Brandenburg-Prussia switched sides at the Treaty of Bromberg (6 November 1657).

wars.name: First Partition of Poland

zones.text: Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn, annexed by Prussia in 1772

wars.outcome: Prussia took most of Royal Prussia, with Warmia, the Netze District and northern Kuyavia, not Danzig and Thorn.

certainty.note: The 1466 frontier with the Order and the voivodeship boundaries are treaty and administrative lines, but the pages give no survey; the drawn shape follows modern voivodeship boundaries and polygons, with the western Pomeranian edge, the Chełmno-Greater Poland line and the Marienwerder edge approximate.

notes:
Royal Prussia is a state Cliopatria lacks (eu-14-f and eu-14-x flagged it). Typed colony: the page calls it 'an autonomous province of the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland'; the colour agent can draw it as a tint of the Polish row (kingdom-of-poland, then polish-lithuanian-commonwealth from 1569). Start follows the infobox (19 October 1466); the Prussian Confederation (rebel, 1454-1466) holds the same land before it.

Repaired after the review (2026-10-31). The gazetteer region 'West Prussia' (alt name 'Royal Prussia') is Pomeranian + Kuyavian-Pomeranian and was the wrong stand-in: it left Elbląg out and drew Włocławek, Inowrocław, Bydgoszcz, Słupsk and Lębork. The shape is now built from the Pomeranian voivodeship, a Chełmno Land polygon in the Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship and a disc at Elbląg (see the keyframe note), about 21,250 km2; the same spec is used in every ledger region, in identity and in wars. Warmia is left to prince-bishopric-of-warmia and Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) to the Teutonic remainder / Ducal Prussia; the Lauenburg and Bütow Land is drawn only 1637-1657 (keyframes 1637 and 1657, events 1637 and 1657). Swedish occupations 1626-1635 and 1655-1660 added as occupation events (the owner's record; kingdom-of-sweden books the mirror).

Where I disagree with the reviewer: the review says Lębork and Bytów are not Royal Prussia. The Royal Prussia page lists the 'Lauenburg and Bütow Land' among its territories, and the Lauenburg and Bütow Land and Pomeranian Voivodeship pages put it in the voivodeship from 1637 (or 1641) to 1657 only; before 1637 it was a fief of the Griffin dukes and after 1657 of Brandenburg. So it is out of the core shape and in for 1637-1656, which the reviewer's polygon fix did not cover.

Not settled: (1) no capital: three pages opened (Royal Prussia 'Capital(s): Not stated', Pomeranian Voivodeship, Gdańsk) do not say where the Prussian council or Landtag sat; the voivodeship seat Skarszewy (from 1613) is not the province's. identity.capitals stays empty. (2) Danzig and Thorn 1772-1793: the Royal Prussia page does not say they stayed Polish; the First Partition page says Prussia did not take them; the Gdańsk page says Danzig 'remained a part of Poland as an exclave'. (3) The 1 July 1772 infobox date precedes the 5 August 1772 treaty on the First Partition page; the month is the infobox's. (4) The Netze District and northern Kuyavia that Prussia also took in 1772 are Great Poland land, not Royal Prussia; see west-prussia. (5) Warmia is counted in the former Royal Prussia by the page; drawn as its own dossier. (6) The Swedish events rest on the war pages; the exact dates of individual towns in 1626 and the return of Elbląg and Malbork in 1660 are not on the pages. The Truce of Altmark page (26 September 1629) and the war page (6 September 1629) disagree on the day. (7) The 1525 secularisation of the Order (Duchy of Prussia under Polish overlordship) is the neighbouring duchy's event. (8) The gazetteer needs regions 'Royal Prussia' (distinct from 'West Prussia'), 'Chełmno Land' and 'Lauenburg and Bütow Land'.
